Light.MergeSort.clog_split.natural_language_statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n\ge2$, set $h=\lceil n/2\rceil=(n+1)\mathbin{/}2$, and write $L(k)=\operatorname{clog}_2(k)$ for the natural ceiling logarithm. Then

$$hL(h)+(n-h)L(n-h)+n\le nL(n).$$

This finite inequality pays for two recursively sorted halves and a linear merge within the usual $n\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ budget.

Light.neg_emod_nat.natural_language_statement:
Let $a,M\in\mathbb N$ with $M\ge1$, and let $r=a\bmod M$ be the natural-number remainder. Interpreting $-a$ and $M$ as integers, their Euclidean remainder satisfies

$$(-a)\bmod M=\begin{cases}0,&r=0,\\M-r,&r\ne0.\end{cases}$$

This identity converts a remainder routine for nonnegative inputs into the corresponding calculation for negative inputs.

ThreeSum.Arithmetic.early_yes.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.Arithmetic.early_yes : ∀ {ι : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype.{u_2} τ] [inst_1 : DecidableEq.{u_2 + 1} τ] (I : Finset.{u_1} ι)
  (owner : ι → τ) (weight : ι → Nat) (good : τ → Prop) [inst_2 : @DecidablePred.{u_2 + 1} τ good] (Rmax H : Nat)
  (hcap :
    ∀ (t : τ),
      Not (good t) →
        @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@ThreeSum.Arithmetic.fiberWeight.{u_1, u_2} ι τ inst_1 I owner weight t) Rmax)
  (hcount : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@Finset.card.{u_2} τ {t : τ | Not (good t)}) H)
  (hlarge :
    @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) Rmax H)
      (∑ i ∈ I, weight i)),
  ∃ (i : ι),
    And
      (@Membership.mem.{u_1, u_1} ι (Finset.{u_1} ι)
        (@SetLike.instMembership.{u_1, u_1} (Finset.{u_1} ι) ι (@Finset.instSetLike.{u_1} ι)) I i)
      (And (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))) (weight i))
        (good (owner i))) := by
  sorry
ThreeSum.Arithmetic.early_yes.natural_language_statement:
Let $I$ be a finite set of incidences, $\tau$ a finite owner set, $o:I\to\tau$ the owner map, and $w_i\in\mathbb N$ the incidence weights. Let $G\subseteq\tau$ be the good owners, and let $R,H\in\mathbb N$. Suppose each bad owner has fiber weight at most $R$, and there are at most $H$ bad owners:

$$\sum_{i\in I:\,o(i)=t}w_i\le R\quad(t\notin G),\qquad |\tau\setminus G|\le H.$$

If $\sum_{i\in I}w_i>RH$, then

$$\exists i\in I:\quad w_i>0\ \land\ o(i)\in G.$$

This counting criterion justifies an early positive answer when represented mass exceeds the maximum mass attributable to false original candidates.

          (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHMul.{0} Int Int.instMul) u m)

        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 1) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 1)))),
  Iff (@Dvd.dvd.{0} Int Int.instDvd (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHMul.{0} Int Int.instMul) m l) x)
    (And (@Dvd.dvd.{0} Int Int.instDvd m x) (@Dvd.dvd.{0} Int Int.instDvd l x)) := by

ThreeSum.Arithmetic.mul_dvd_iff_of_bezou.natural_language_statement:
Let $m,\ell,x\in\mathbb Z$. Suppose there are integers $u,v$ with $um+v\ell=1$. Then

$$m\ell\mid x\iff(m\mid x\ \land\ \ell\mid x).$$

The hypothesis is a concrete Bézout certificate; no positivity or primality assumption is required. The equivalence combines separate divisibility tests into one test for the product modulus.

  (ha0 : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 0) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 0))) a)
  (haP : @LT.lt.{0} Int Int.instLTInt a P)
  (hb0 : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 0) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 0))) b)
  (hbP : @LT.lt.{0} Int Int.instLTInt b P)
  (hc0 : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 0) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 0))) c)
  (hcP : @LT.lt.{0} Int Int.instLTInt c P)
  (hdiv :
    @Dvd.dvd.{0} Int Int.instDvd P
      (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHSub.{0} Int Int.instSub)
        (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHSub.{0} Int Int.instSub) c b) a)),
  ∃ (j : Int),
    And (ThreeSum.Arithmetic.SmallLift j)
      (@Eq.{1} Int (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHSub.{0} Int Int.instSub) c b)
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHAdd.{0} Int Int.instAdd) a
          (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHMul.{0} Int Int.instMul) j P))) := by
  sorry
ThreeSum.Arithmetic.small_lift_exists.natural_language_statement:
Let $P,a,b,c\in\mathbb Z$ satisfy $P>0$ and $0\le a,b,c<P$. Assume $P\mid(c-b-a)$, so these canonical residues satisfy the required modular relation. Then

$$\exists j\in\{-1,0,1\}:\qquad c-b=a+jP.$$

Thus the fixed three-element signed-lift list covers every modular candidate formed from canonical residues. The statement supplies the completeness direction needed when modular relations are represented by a short list of integer equations.

theorem ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.fromOwner_sound : ∀ (A B C : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Family) (o : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Owner A B C)
  (hf :
    @Eq.{1} Nat (ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.fromOwner A B C o).flag
      (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1)))),
  have r := ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.fromOwner A B C o;
  And (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat r.a A.size)
    (And (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat r.b B.size)
      (And (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat r.c C.size)
        (@ThreeSum.Bands.Relevant.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat A.lower A.upper B.lower B.upper C.lower C.upper
          (@Prod.mk.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat) r.a (@Prod.mk.{0, 0} Nat Nat r.b r.c))))) := by
  sorry
ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.fromOwner_sou.natural_language_statement:
Let $A,B,C$ be finite ordered families of nonempty, pairwise separated integer intervals. An owner specifies an in-range $BC$, $AB$, or $AC$ index pair. Construct its record by looking up the missing interval at $C_k^--B_j^+$, $A_i^-+B_j^-$, or $C_k^--A_i^-$, respectively, encoding a successful lookup with flag one. If the resulting record $r=(\mathrm{flag},a,b,c)$ has $\mathrm{flag}=1$, then

$$
\begin{gathered}
a<|A|,\qquad b<|B|,\qquad c<|C|,\\
A_a^-+B_b^-\le C_c^+,\qquad C_c^-\le A_a^++B_b^+.
\end{gathered}
$$

Equivalently, its indices are valid and its band triple is relevant. This ensures that accepted physical candidate records satisfy the interval condition used in later counting and reporting arguments.

ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.mem_records_o.theorem_title: Every physical band record comes from an owner
ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.mem_records_o.natural_language_statement:
Let $A,B,C$ be finite families of sorted, separated integer intervals. Their owner set is the disjoint union of the $BC$, $AB$, and $AC$ index rectangles. Let $\mathcal R(A,B,C)$ be the record list obtained by enumerating these rectangles in that order, and let $\rho(o)$ be the record produced by an owner $o$. For any record $r$,

$$r\in\mathcal R(A,B,C)\ \Longrightarrow\ \exists o:\ \rho(o)=r.$$

The statement applies to all catalog records, including lookup misses. It connects membership in the physical record list to the abstract owner-indexed representation.

ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Family.lookup_s.theorem_title: Successful interval lookup returns a containing band
ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Family.lookup_s.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Family.lookup_sound : ∀ (A : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Family) (x : Int) (i : A.Index)
  (h : @Eq.{1} (Option.{0} A.Index) (A.lookup x) (@Option.some.{0} A.Index i)),
  And (@LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (A.lo i) x) (@LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt x (A.hi i)) := by
  sorry
ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Family.lookup_s.natural_language_statement:
Let $A$ be a finite family of integer intervals $[\ell_i,u_i]$, indexed by $0\le i<N$. Assume each interval is nonempty, the lower endpoints are nondecreasing, and $u_i<\ell_j$ whenever $i<j<N$. For $x\in\mathbb Z$ and an in-range index $i$, if the family's binary-search lookup returns $i$, then

$$
\operatorname{lookup}_A(x)=\operatorname{some}(i)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \ell_i\le x\le u_i.
$$

The lookup includes a check that its returned index lies in the family.

This supplies the interval-containment guarantee for successful band-candidate lookups.

ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.candidate_owner.theorem_title: Every relevant band triple is recovered from its selected owner
ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.candidate_owner.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.candidate_owner : ∀ (A B C : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Family) (t : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Triple A B C)
  (ht : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.relevant A B C t),
  @Eq.{1} (Option.{0} (ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Triple A B C))
    (ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.candidate A B C (ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.owner A B C t))
    (@Option.some.{0} (ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Triple A B C) t) := by
  sorry
ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.candidate_owner.natural_language_statement:
Let $A,B,C$ be finite families of nonempty, ordered, pairwise separated integer intervals, with endpoints $A_i^-,A_i^+$ and similarly for $B,C$. Let $(i,j,k)$ be in-range indices satisfying
$A_i^-+B_j^-\le C_k^+$ and $C_k^-\le A_i^++B_j^+$. Select its owner as $BC(j,k)$ if $A_i^-<C_k^--B_j^+$; otherwise choose $AC(i,k)$ when $A_i^-+B_j^-\le C_k^-$ and $AB(i,j)$ in the remaining case. The candidate operation reconstructs the missing index by interval lookup at, respectively, $C_k^--B_j^+$, $C_k^--A_i^-$, or $A_i^-+B_j^-$. Then

$$
\operatorname{candidate}(\operatorname{owner}(i,j,k))
=\operatorname{some}(i,j,k).
$$

Thus the quadratic owner catalog includes every relevant triple of bands.

  (hy : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))) y)
  (hprime : ∀ (i : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i s → Nat.Prime (primes i))
  (hinj :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i s →
        ∀ (j : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j s → @Eq.{1} Nat (primes i) (primes j) → @Eq.{1} Nat i j)
  (hlo : ∀ (i : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i s → @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat y (primes i))
  (hA :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i nA →
        @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup (A i))
          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt U))
  (hB :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i nB →
        @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup (B i))
          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt U))
  (hC :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i nC →
        @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup (C i))
          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt U)),
  @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
      (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
        (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid))) s r)
      (ThreeSum.BandWeightedScore.score primes s (ThreeSum.BandPrimeChoice.modulus primes s nA nB nC g A B C rs r) nA nB
        nC g A B C rs))
    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
      (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat

        (Nat.log y

            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 3) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 3))) U))
        r)

ThreeSum.BandPrimeChoice.modulus_score_b.natural_language_statement:
Let $(p_i)_{i\in\mathbb N}$ be a natural-number sequence whose first $s$ entries are distinct primes at least $y>1$. Let $A,B,C$ be integer arrays of lengths $n_A,n_B,n_C$ with absolute values at most a natural number $U$, and let $g,r$ be natural numbers. Fix a list of band-owner records, each with three band indices and a flag. For modulus $q$, let $S(q)$ sum, over records flagged $1$ and triples in their truncated bands, the indicator of $q\mid\delta$ times the number of pool primes not dividing $\delta$, where $\delta=C(c)-B(b)-A(a)$. Repeated records retain their multiplicity.

Set $q_0=1$ and choose $q_{k+1}=q_kp_i$ using the least-index minimizer of $S(q_kp_i)$ among the pool, with index zero for an empty pool. Then
$$s^rS(q_r)\le\bigl(\operatorname{log}^{\mathbb N}_y(3U)\bigr)^rS(1),$$
where the integer logarithm is zero at argument zero.

This establishes contraction for one modulus sequence shared by the complete owner catalog.

ThreeSum.BandPrimeCosts.aggregate_time_l.natural_language_statement:
Let $p,g,R,s,U\in\mathbb N$ be, respectively, the modulus bound, band-size bound, number of owner records, number of auxiliary primes, and input-magnitude bound. Write $T_{\mathrm{count}}(p,g,g,g,U)$ for the modular-counting budget and $T_{\mathrm{joint}}(p)$ for the auxiliary modulus budget. Set $u(p,g,U)=T_{\mathrm{count}}(p,g,g,g,U)+T_{\mathrm{joint}}(p)+1000$. The aggregate weighted-score budget satisfies

$$T_{\mathrm{aggregate}}(p,g,R,s,U)\le2(R+1)(s+1)u(p,g,U).$$

This is an unconditional inequality between the defined natural-number budgets. It charges the catalog scan and its fixed overhead to the same unit used for each scoring call.

theorem ThreeSum.BandPrimeCosts.pool_time_le : ∀ (y : Nat),

      (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 100000) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 100000)))

        (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid)))
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) y
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 3) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 3))))) := by

ThreeSum.BandPrimeCosts.pool_time_le.natural_language_statement:
For a natural parameter $y$, let $T_{\mathrm{pool}}(y)$ be the defined execution budget of the routine that scans $(y,4y]$ and tests candidates by trial division. Then, for every $y\in\mathbb N$,

$$T_{\mathrm{pool}}(y)\le100000(y+1)^3.$$

This finite bound includes the small-parameter cases and accounts for prime-pool generation in the complete common-prime setup budget.

ThreeSum.BandRawA.firstRows_getD.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandRawA.firstRows_getD : ∀ {n g s i j : Nat} {rs : List.{0} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record} (hs : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat s i)
  (hj :
    @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j
      (@List.length.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label
        (ThreeSum.BandRawA.row n g s
          (@List.getD.{0} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record rs s
            (@Inhabited.default.{1} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record
              ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.instInhabitedRecord))))),
  @Eq.{1} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label
    (@List.getD.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label (ThreeSum.BandRawA.firstRows n g rs i)
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) (ThreeSum.BandRawA.count n g rs s) j)
      (@Inhabited.default.{1} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label ThreeSum.BandRawA.instInhabitedLabel))
    { owner := s,
      position :=
        @HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
          (ThreeSum.BandPartition.start g
            (@List.getD.{0} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record rs s
                (@Inhabited.default.{1} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record
                  ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.instInhabitedRecord)).a)
          j } := by
  sorry
ThreeSum.BandRawA.firstRows_getD.natural_language_statement:
Let $n,g,s,i,j\in\mathbb N$ and let $\mathcal R$ be a list of band records. Use a zero record for any index beyond its length. Let $L_t$ be row $t$: when that record is active, its labels are $(t,ga_t+q)$ for positions in its truncated A band; otherwise it is empty. Let $F_i=L_0\mathbin{+\!+}\cdots\mathbin{+\!+}L_{i-1}$ and $C_s=\sum_{t<s}|L_t|$. If $s<i$ and $j<|L_s|$, then

$$(F_i)_{C_s+j}=(s,ga_s+j).$$

This indexing identity records both the physical owner slot and the original A-array coordinate of each emitted incidence.

ThreeSum.BandRawA.mem_aIndices_iff_owner.theorem_title: Physical A-incidence indices are exactly their owner fiber
ThreeSum.BandRawA.mem_aIndices_iff_owner.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandRawA.mem_aIndices_iff_owner : ∀ {n g s k : Nat} {rs : List.{0} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record}
  (hs : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat s (@List.length.{0} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record rs)),
  Iff
    (@Membership.mem.{0, 0} Nat (Finset.{0} Nat)
      (@SetLike.instMembership.{0, 0} (Finset.{0} Nat) Nat (@Finset.instSetLike.{0} Nat))
      (ThreeSum.BandRawA.aIndices n g rs s) k)
    (And (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat k (@List.length.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label (ThreeSum.BandRawA.items n g rs)))
      (@Eq.{1} Nat (ThreeSum.BandRawA.labelAt n g rs k).owner s)) := by
  sorry
ThreeSum.BandRawA.mem_aIndices_iff_owner.natural_language_statement:
Let $n,g\in\mathbb N$ and let $R$ be a list of band-owner records. The physical A-incidence list concatenates, for each record flagged one, its truncated A-band positions, labeling every entry with its owner slot. For a valid slot $s<|R|$, let $A_s$ be the contiguous set of physical indices contributed by that record, and let $I$ be the entire incidence list. Then, for any $k\in\mathbb N$,

$$
k\in A_s\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad k<|I|\ \land\ \operatorname{owner}(I_k)=s.
$$

This exactly identifies each owner's counting domain while retaining separate physical incidences for different owners, even when their values agree.

Write $B_r$ and $C_r$ for that record's original B- and C-band positions, using the intervals $[bg,\min(n_B,(b+1)g))$ and $[cg,\min(n_C,(c+1)g))$. Let $\mathcal P$ be the union, over record slots, of the corresponding physical A-label positions crossed with these B and C bands. For every natural triple $(i,j,k)$,

$$
(i,j,k)\in\mathcal P\iff i<|I|\ \land\ j\in B_{o(i)}\ \land\ k\in C_{o(i)}.
$$

This identifies the exact domain represented by the physical owner catalog.

Let $n,g,o\in\mathbb N$, let $r$ be a band record with flag $r_f$ and A-band index $r_a$, and let $\lambda=(\lambda_o,\lambda_x)$ be an owner-position label. The row generated by $r$ for owner $o$ contains exactly the labels specified by

ThreeSum.BandRawA.owner_weightedFalseCou.natural_language_statement:
Let $A,B,C$ be integer arrays with natural lengths $n_A,n_B,n_C$, let $g$ be the band size, and let $R$ be a record list with $s<|R|$. Let $p:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, $a,q\in\mathbb N$, and let $\Lambda=\{p(i):i<a\}$ be the auxiliary modulus set. Define $w(z)=|\{\ell\in\Lambda:\ell\nmid z\}|$. Let $\mathcal P_s$ pair the physical A-incidence indices owned by $s$ with that record's B- and C-band positions; write $\widetilde A$ for the corresponding physical values. Then

$$
\sum_{\substack{(i,j,k)\in\mathcal P_s\\q\mid C_k-B_j-\widetilde A_i}}w(C_k-B_j-\widetilde A_i)=\operatorname{blockScore}(R_s).
$$

The block score is the same weighted count on the three original truncated bands when the flag is one, and zero otherwise. No primality or injectivity hypothesis on $p$ is needed for this identity.

Let $A,B,C$ be finite integer lists, $g\in\mathbb N$, and $R$ any list of band records carrying flags. Form the raw-A incidence list by concatenating each flagged record's truncated A band, retaining the physical owner and source position. Let $\mathcal P$ be the union of the corresponding physical A-index, original B-band, and original C-band products. $$
a_i\in A,\qquad B.\operatorname{getD}(j,0)\in B,\qquad C.\operatorname{getD}(k,0)\in C.
$$

The lookup notation supplies zero only for an out-of-range index; membership in $\mathcal P$ guarantees that these accesses are in range.

This connects physical owner-product coordinates to membership in the retained source lists.

ThreeSum.BandRawA.relevant_product_compl.theorem_title: Every relevant band product appears in its physical owner domain
ThreeSum.BandRawA.relevant_product_compl.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandRawA.relevant_product_complete : ∀ {A B C : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Family} {nA nB nC g pA pB pC : Nat} (t : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Triple A B C)
  (ht : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.relevant A B C t)
  (ha :
    And
      (@LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
        (ThreeSum.BandPartition.start g (@Fin.val A.size (@Prod.fst.{0, 0} A.Index (Prod.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index) t)))
        pA)
      (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat pA
        (ThreeSum.BandPartition.stop nA g
          (@Fin.val A.size (@Prod.fst.{0, 0} A.Index (Prod.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index) t)))))
  (hb :
    And
      (@LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
        (ThreeSum.BandPartition.start g
          (@Fin.val B.size
            (@Prod.fst.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index (@Prod.snd.{0, 0} A.Index (Prod.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index) t))))
        pB)
      (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat pB
        (ThreeSum.BandPartition.stop nB g
          (@Fin.val B.size
            (@Prod.fst.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index (@Prod.snd.{0, 0} A.Index (Prod.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index) t))))))
  (hc :
    And
      (@LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
        (ThreeSum.BandPartition.start g
          (@Fin.val C.size
            (@Prod.snd.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index (@Prod.snd.{0, 0} A.Index (Prod.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index) t))))
        pC)
      (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat pC
        (ThreeSum.BandPartition.stop nC g
          (@Fin.val C.size
            (@Prod.snd.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index (@Prod.snd.{0, 0} A.Index (Prod.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index) t)))))),
  ∃ (k : Nat),
    And
      (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat k
        (@List.length.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label
          (ThreeSum.BandRawA.items nA g (ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.records A B C))))
      (And
        (@Eq.{1} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label (ThreeSum.BandRawA.labelAt nA g (ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.records A B C) k)
          { owner := ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.slot A B C (ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.owner A B C t), position := pA })
        (@Membership.mem.{0, 0} (Prod.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat))
          (Finset.{0} (Prod.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat)))
          (@SetLike.instMembership.{0, 0} (Finset.{0} (Prod.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat)))
            (Prod.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat)) (@Finset.instSetLike.{0} (Prod.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat))))
          (ThreeSum.BandRawA.ownerProduct nA nB nC g (ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.records A B C)
            (ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.slot A B C (ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.owner A B C t)))
          (@Prod.mk.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat) k (@Prod.mk.{0, 0} Nat Nat pB pC)))) := by
  sorry
ThreeSum.BandRawA.relevant_product_compl.natural_language_statement:
Let $A,B,C$ be finite, ordered families of nonempty, pairwise separated integer intervals. Let $t=(i,j,\ell)$ satisfy $A_i^{\rm lo}+B_j^{\rm lo}\le C_\ell^{\rm hi}$ and $C_\ell^{\rm lo}\le A_i^{\rm hi}+B_j^{\rm hi}$. For natural lengths $n_A,n_B,n_C$ and band width $g$, choose positions $p_A,p_B,p_C$ in the corresponding half-open index bands $[ag,\min(n,(a+1)g))$. Let $r$ be the canonical owner-record list, $s$ the physical slot of the owner of $t$, and $I$ its flattened $A$-incidence list. Then
$$
\exists k<|I|:\quad \operatorname{label}(k)=(s,p_A),\qquad
(k,p_B,p_C)\in\operatorname{ownerProduct}(r,s).
$$
Here the owner product combines that owner's physical $A$ indices with its original $B/C$ positions. Thus every relevant coordinate triple is retained with its physical incidence identity.

ThreeSum.BandWeightedScore.block_bound.theorem_title: Uniform weighted-score bound for one band-owner block
ThreeSum.BandWeightedScore.block_bound.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandWeightedScore.block_bound : ∀ (primes : Nat → Nat) (s q nA nB nC g : Nat) (A B C : Nat → Int) (r : ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record)
  (hprime : ∀ (i : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i s → Nat.Prime (primes i))
  (hinj :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i s →
        ∀ (j : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j s → @Eq.{1} Nat (primes i) (primes j) → @Eq.{1} Nat i j),
  @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (ThreeSum.BandWeightedScore.block primes s q nA nB nC g A B C r)
    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) s
      (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
        (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid))) g
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 3) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 3))))) := by
  sorry
ThreeSum.BandWeightedScore.block_bound.natural_language_statement:
Let $A,B,C:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ have declared lengths $n_A,n_B,n_C$, let $g,s,q\in\mathbb N$, and let $p_0,\ldots,p_{s-1}$ be distinct primes. A record $r=(\mathrm{flag},a,b,c)$ selects the three truncated bands starting at $ag,bg,cg$, each of length at most $g$. Its block score is zero unless $\mathrm{flag}=1$; otherwise it sums, over triples in those bands with $q\mid C_k-B_j-A_i$, the number of selected primes that do not divide $C_k-B_j-A_i$. Then

$$
\operatorname{block}(p,s,q,n_A,n_B,n_C,g,A,B,C,r)\le s g^3.
$$

All lengths and the base modulus may be zero. This is the uniform initial charge for each physical candidate record, retaining catalog multiplicities.

ThreeSum.BinarySearch.locate_complete.theorem_title: Interval lookup finds every containing separated interval
ThreeSum.BinarySearch.locate_complete.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BinarySearch.locate_complete : ∀ (lo hi : Nat → Int) (n : Nat) (x : Int)
  (hsorted :
    ∀ (i j : Nat),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat i j → @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j n → @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (lo i) (lo j))
  (hseparated :
    ∀ (i j : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i j → @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j n → @LT.lt.{0} Int Int.instLTInt (hi i) (lo j))
  {i : Nat} (hin : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i n) (hil : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (lo i) x)
  (hih : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt x (hi i)),
  @Eq.{1} (Option.{0} Nat) (ThreeSum.BinarySearch.locate lo hi n x) (@Option.some.{0} Nat i) := by
  sorry
ThreeSum.BinarySearch.locate_complete.natural_language_statement:
Let $\ell,h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ describe $n$ closed intervals. Suppose their lower endpoints are nondecreasing, and whenever $i<j<n$ the strict separation $h(i)<\ell(j)$ holds. If $i<n$ and $\ell(i)\le x\le h(i)$, then the binary-search interval locator returns

$$
\operatorname{locate}(\ell,h,n,x)=\operatorname{some}(i).
$$

The locator first finds the upper-bound position among the lower endpoints and then checks the preceding interval's upper endpoint. This establishes completeness of the interval access used to identify a matching band.

ThreeSum.BinarySearch.locate_sound.natural_language_statement:
Let $\ell,h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$, let $n\in\mathbb N$, and assume $\ell$ is nondecreasing on indices below $n$. For an integer query $x$, if the binary-search interval locator returns index $i$, then

$$
\operatorname{locate}(\ell,h,n,x)=\operatorname{some}(i)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad i<n\ \land\ \ell(i)\le x\le h(i).
$$

No separation assumption on the intervals is needed for this soundness result. It certifies every successful band lookup even before uniqueness or completeness is used.

ThreeSum.BinarySearch.upperSearch_correc.natural_language_statement:
Let $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ be nondecreasing on its first $n$ entries, and let $x\in\mathbb Z$. Choose natural numbers $b,\ell,h$ with $\ell\le h\le n$ and $h-\ell<2^b$. Assume every index below $\ell$ has value at most $x$, and every index from $h$ to $n-1$ has value strictly above $x$. If $k$ is the result of the upper-bound search with fuel $b$ and interval $[\ell,h)$, then

$$
k\le n,\qquad (\forall i<k,\ f(i)\le x),\qquad (\forall k\le i<n,\ x<f(i)).
$$

Thus the bounded search returns the correct partition point, including when the result is the end of the array.

Let $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ be memory, with array bases $d_0,d_1$, and let $J,L,p\in\mathbb N$. Let $s:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ select rows and let $w_0,w_1:\mathbb N^2\to\mathbb N$ be their coefficients. Assume the stored row invariant: for $a<J$, $b<L$, and $e\in\{0,1\}$, memory at $d_e+aL+b$ contains $p^a w_e(s(a),b)$. Define the flattened function by $F_e(aL+b)=p^a w_e(s(a),b)$ on the $JL$ positions. Then

$$
\forall e\in\{0,1\}\ \forall i<JL,\qquad \mu(d_e+i)=F_e(i).
$$

The equality identifies the constructor's row layout with the flat array read by the mask evaluator, including empty dimensions.

Let $J,L\in\mathbb N$, let $I\subseteq\{0,\ldots,J-1\}$, and let $Q_i,u_i\subseteq\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$. Define $P_L=\{(i,a):i\in I,\ a\in u_i\}$, $P_R=\{(i,a):i\in I,\ a\in Q_i\setminus u_i\}$, and $R=\{(i,a):i\notin I,\ a\in Q_i\}$. For every $X\subseteq R$,

$$
(P_L\cup X)\cap(P_R\cup(R\setminus X))=\varnothing.
$$

No containment assumption on the $u_i$ is required for this disjointness claim. Together with the corresponding coverage identity, it supports the exact left/right decomposition used in prefix reporting.

Let $J,L,k\in\mathbb N$ with $k\le J$. View the coordinates as pairs $(i,a)$ with $i<J$ and $a<L$, flattened by the row-major index $iL+a$. The suffix domain after fixing the first $k$ blocks consists of all pairs with $i\ge k$. Its image is

$$
\{iL+a:k\le i<J,\ 0\le a<L\}=\{q\in\mathbb N:kL\le q<JL\}.
$$

Equivalently, this is the subset-transform suffix of length $(J-k)L$ in the ground set of size $JL$. The identity aligns the block reporting query with the contiguous suffix processed by the stored transform stages.

ThreeSum.BooleanGreedy.choice_eq_least.theorem_title: Greedy row selection equals the scan of negated scores
ThreeSum.BooleanGreedy.choice_eq_least.natural_language_statement:
Let $M:\mathbb N^2\to\mathbb N$ have $R>0$ rows and $C$ columns, with $M_{ij}\le1$ for valid row and column indices. Let $a_t(j)$ indicate whether column $j$ remains uncovered after $t$ greedy steps, and define the row score $s_t(i)=\sum_{j<C}M_{ij}a_t(j)$. Then

$$
\operatorname{choice}(M,R,C,t)=\operatorname{least}_{i<R}\bigl(-s_t(i)\bigr).
$$

The right side is the left-to-right integer minimum scan, retaining the earliest index on ties. This identifies the finite greedy covering choice with the score computation and scan used by the implementation.

ThreeSum.Cover.greedyState_geometric.natural_language_statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty collection of maps, supplied as a list containing every map, and let $T$ be a finite target set in a type with decidable equality. Let the covering relation be decidable. Suppose $a\in\mathbb N$ is positive and every $u\in T$ is covered by at least a $1/a$ fraction of $\Omega$, in the integer form $|\Omega|\le a|\{\omega:\omega\text{ covers }u\}|$. Let $G_t$ be the targets left after $t$ greedy steps, each selecting a map covering the most remaining targets. Then

$$
a^t|G_t|\le(a-1)^t|T|\qquad(t\in\mathbb N).
$$

This denominator-free estimate turns a uniform coverage frequency into a bound on the deterministic greedy schedule length.

ThreeSum.Cover.greedy_cover.natural_language_statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty finite set of maps, supplied by a list containing every element, and let $T$ be a finite target set. Assume coverage is decidable. For an integer $a>1$, suppose each target is covered by at least a $1/a$ fraction of all maps:

$$|\Omega|\le a\,|\{\omega\in\Omega:\omega\text{ covers }u\}|\qquad(u\in T).$$

$$\forall u\in T,\quad\exists\omega\in G_m:\omega\text{ covers }u.$$

This proves a finite cover bound for the actual executable selection rule, allowing repeated maps in the input or output lists.

Let $p\in\mathbb N$ be positive, let $F,H:\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z\to\mathbb N$, and let $0\le r<p$. Form integer coefficient vectors $A_i=F(i)$ and $B_i=H(-i)$ for $0\le i<p$. Their cyclic convolution satisfies

$$
\sum_{\substack{0\le i,j<p\\i+j\equiv r\pmod p}}A_iB_j
=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z}F(z)H(z-r).
$$

The right side is the defined modular correlation, embedded in the integers. Primality of $p$ is not assumed. This identity connects the dense polynomial-product computation to the correlation used for balancing.

$$
\bigl|\{f\in E:\ell_f=\ell_e\ \text{or}\ r_f=r_e\ \text{or}\ m_f=m_e\}\bigr|
\le 2\Delta+G.
$$

The three classes may overlap, and the count includes $e$ itself when applicable.

This controls the exceptional partner pairs that require separate treatment in the hash-family second-moment estimate.

ThreeSum.HashFamily.four_relation_of_mas.natural_language_statement:
Let $K$ be a ring and let $s,t,u,v:\alpha\to\{0,1\}$ be four pairwise distinct Boolean words. For a word $z$, define $e_z(i,b)=1$ if $z_i=b$ and zero otherwise. Suppose the equality masks of the pairs differ at some coordinate: $[s_i=t_i]\ne[u_i=v_i]$. If $a,b,c,d\in K$ satisfy

$$a e_s(p)+b e_t(p)+c e_u(p)+d e_v(p)=0\qquad\text{for every }p\in\alpha\times\{0,1\},$$

then

$$a=b=c=d=0.$$

This isolates the only possible four-endpoint dependence relevant to the hash moments: distinct equality masks cannot support a nontrivial relation.

ThreeSum.HashFamily.hashMap_surjective.natural_language_statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let $I$ and $S$ be finite sets, and let $(v_i)_{i\in I}$ be a linearly independent family in $K^S$. The hash map sends a weight vector $w\in K^S$ to the vector whose $i$th entry is $\sum_{x\in S}v_i(x)w(x)$. Every target vector is attained:

$$
\forall t\in K^I,\ \exists w\in K^S,\ \forall i\in I,
\qquad \sum_{x\in S}v_i(x)w(x)=t(i).
$$

The field itself need not be finite.

This proves that the concrete coefficient construction can realize all prescribed hash outputs, providing the linear-algebraic input for the later exact fiber counts.

ThreeSum.HashFamily.heavyPairEvent_bound.natural_language_statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite coordinate set and $K$ a finite field of cardinality $q$. For a weight assignment $w:\alpha\times\{0,1\}\to K$, define $H_w(u)=\sum_{i\in\alpha}w(i,u_i)$. Fix distinct binary words $s,t$, arbitrary targets $a,b\in K$, and a finite set $V$ of binary words with $t\notin V$. Let $B$ be a natural number satisfying $4(q+|V|)\le Bq$. For
$$E=\{w:H_w(s)=a,\ H_w(t)=b,\ |\{u\in V:H_w(u)=a\}|>B\},$$
one has
$$4q^2|E|\le q^{2|\alpha|}.$$

This uniform counting bound controls the loss caused by discarding an oversized bucket, even when $s$ itself belongs to $V$ or the two targets coincide.

Let $\alpha$ be a finite coordinate set and $K$ a finite field of size $q$, with decidable equality. Let $\mathcal W=K^{\alpha\times\{0,1\}}$, and define $H_w(z)=\sum_{i\in\alpha}w(i,z_i)$. $$q^3|E_{s,t}\cap E_{u,v}|\le|\mathcal W|.$$

Endpoints within the same class may coincide. This joint-event bound provides the cubic denominator used for potentially dependent edge pairs in the second moment.

ThreeSum.HashFamily.linear_fiber_card.natural_language_statement:
Let $K$ be a field and let $V,W$ be $K$-vector spaces with finite underlying sets. If $f:V\to W$ is a surjective linear map, then for every target $y\in W$,

$$
|W|\,\bigl|f^{-1}(\{y\})\bigr|=|V|.
$$

The statement counts the full domain and every target fiber as natural numbers. It does not require a separate assumption that the field is finite.

This is the exact counting form of uniformity for a surjective linear map: uniform enumeration of domain elements gives equal multiplicity to every target. It is used to establish finite hash-output probabilities without approximate counting.

ThreeSum.HashFamily.loadedPairMass_bound.natural_language_statement:
Let $\alpha$ be finite, let $K$ be a finite field of size $q$, and use all coefficient functions $\mathcal W=K^{\alpha\times\{0,1\}}$ with one-hot hash $H_w$. Fix distinct Boolean words $s,t$, targets $a,b\in K$, and a finite vertex set $V$ with $t\notin V$. Set $E=\{w:H_w(s)=a,\ H_w(t)=b\}$ and $B_w=|\{u\in V:H_w(u)=a\}|$. Then

$$q^3\sum_{w\in E}B_w\le(q+|V|)|\mathcal W|.$$

There is no requirement that $s$ belong to $V$. This controls bucket load under a fixed endpoint-pair event, supporting the separable trimming estimate.

ThreeSum.HashFamily.raw_second_moment.natural_language_statement:
Let $\alpha,E$ be finite types and $K$ a finite field of size $q$. Assign each edge $e\in E$ binary endpoint words $\ell_e,r_e:\alpha\to\{0,1\}$. Assume the ordered endpoint pairs are distinct and $\ell_e\ne r_f$ for every $e,f$. For each $e$, suppose at most $B$ edges $f$ share its left word, share its right word, or have the same coordinatewise equality mask $[\ell_e(i)=r_e(i)]$. For $a,b\in K$ and every weight assignment $w:\alpha\times\{0,1\}\to K$, let $X_w$ count edges with $\sum_iw(i,\ell_e(i))=a$ and $\sum_iw(i,r_e(i))=b$. Writing $m=|E|$ and $\mathcal W=K^{\alpha\times\{0,1\}}$, one has

$$
q^4\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}X_w^2
\le |\mathcal W|\bigl(mq^2+m^2+mBq\bigr).
$$

This controls the second moment by explicitly counting exceptional endpoint dependencies in the actual hash family.

ThreeSum.HashFamily.raw_second_moment_fi.natural_language_statement:
Let $K$ be a finite field of size $p$, $\alpha$ a finite coordinate set, and $E$ a finite edge set. Each edge has binary words $(\ell_e,r_e)$, with distinct ordered pairs and $\ell_e\ne r_f$ for all $e,f$. An edge's bad partners share its left endpoint, right endpoint, or coordinatewise equality mask. Suppose every bad-partner set has size at most $B\le3p$, and $|E|\le p^2$. For $w\in\Omega=K^{\alpha\times\{0,1\}}$, put $H_w(s)=\sum_iw(i,s_i)$ and $X_w=|\{e:H_w(\ell_e)=a,\ H_w(r_e)=b\}|$, where $a,b\in K$. Then
$$
p^2\sum_{w\in\Omega}X_w^2\le5|E|\,|\Omega|.
$$
This supplies the coarse second-moment estimate for the actual one-hot hash family.

ThreeSum.HashFamily.sum_incidenceCount_s.natural_language_statement:
Let $E$ and $\Omega$ be finite sets, and let $A_e\subseteq\Omega$ be an event for each $e\in E$. For $w\in\Omega$, define the incidence count $N(w)=|\{e\in E:w\in A_e\}|$. Then

$$
\sum_{w\in\Omega}N(w)^2
=\sum_{e\in E}\sum_{f\in E}|A_e\cap A_f|.
$$

The right side ranges over ordered pairs, including the diagonal $e=f$. Repeated events are permitted, and no independence assumption is imposed.

This identity expresses the second moment of represented-edge counts through pairwise intersection counts, which can then be evaluated or bounded using the concrete hash family.

ThreeSum.HashFamily.three_relation.natural_language_statement:
Let $K$ be a ring and $A$ any coordinate set. For a binary word $s:A\to\{0,1\}$, define its one-hot encoding by $u_s(i,b)=\mathbf1_{s(i)=b}$, with values in $K$. If $s,t,v$ are pairwise distinct and $a,b,c\in K$ satisfy

$$
a\,u_s(p)+b\,u_t(p)+c\,u_v(p)=0
\quad\text{for every }p\in A\times\{0,1\},
$$

then

$$
a=b=c=0.
$$

No finiteness assumption on the coordinate set is needed.

The result supplies the concrete three-word independence used by the hashing argument; over a field it yields linear independence of these coefficient rows.

ThreeSum.HashFamily.trimmedPairEvent_bou.natural_language_statement:
Let $K$ be a finite field of size $p$, $\alpha$ a finite coordinate set, and $s\ne t$ binary words on $\alpha$. For arbitrary targets $a,b\in K$, take finite word sets $L,R$ with $t\notin L$ and $s\notin R$. Choose a natural cap $B$ satisfying $4(p+|L|)\le Bp$ and $4(p+|R|)\le Bp$. For $H_w(u)=\sum_iw(i,u_i)$, let $T$ contain the weights with $H_w(s)=a$, $H_w(t)=b$, at most $B$ words of $L$ hashing to $a$, and at most $B$ words of $R$ hashing to $b$. Then
$$
|K^{\alpha\times\{0,1\}}|\le2p^2|T|.
$$
Thus separable trimming preserves at least half of the raw pair event, uniformly in the target residues.

      (@ThreeSum.Histograms.histogram.{u_2, u_4} τ G inst_2 J right weightR)

ThreeSum.Histograms.correlation_histogra.natural_language_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $I$ and $J$ be finite index sets. Give each $i\in I$ a key $\ell_i\in G$ and multiplicity $u_i\in\mathbb N$, and each $j\in J$ a key $r_j\in G$ and multiplicity $v_j\in\mathbb N$. Define the histograms $H_L(k)=\sum_{i\in I,\,\ell_i=k}u_i$ and $H_R(k)=\sum_{j\in J,\,r_j=k}v_j$. For every offset $d\in G$,

$$
\sum_{k\in G}H_R(k)H_L(k-d)
=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in J}\mathbf 1_{r_j-\ell_i=d}\,u_i v_j.
$$

Thus correlation gives the exact multiplicity of pairs with the prescribed key difference. The identity supports balancing the actual incidence histograms, including repeated keys and unequal multiplicities.

ThreeSum.Histograms.tripleMass_eq_histog.natural_language_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with decidable equality. Let $A,B,C$ be finite index sets with keys $a_i,b_j,c_k\in G$ and natural weights $u_i,v_j,w_k$. Define $H_B(z)=\sum_{j\in B:b_j=z}v_j$ and $H_C(z)=\sum_{k\in C:c_k=z}w_k$, and let $\operatorname{Corr}(H_C,H_B)(d)=\sum_{z\in G}H_C(z)H_B(z-d)$. Then

$$\sum_{\substack{i\in A,j\in B,k\in C\\a_i+b_j=c_k}}u_i v_j w_k=\sum_{i\in A}u_i\operatorname{Corr}(H_C,H_B)(a_i).$$

A single B/C correlation therefore supports all A-key queries while retaining every multiplicity, including repeated keys.

\operatorname{argmax}_{[0,\ldots,n-1]} f=\operatorname{some}\!\left(\operatorname{least}(-f,n)\right).

          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))) h))
      ((@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))) h).choose

ThreeSum.LayerCounts.edgeSet_card.natural_language_statement:
Let $L,h\in\mathbb N$, and let $E_{L,h}$ be the set of ordered pairs $(S,T)$ of disjoint $h$-element subsets of an $L$-element ground set. Then

$$|E_{L,h}|=\binom{L}{2h}\binom{2h}{h}.$$

The formula includes empty layers when $2h>L$. It gives the exact edge count for the local disjointness graph and separates the number of union outputs from their ordered representations.

ThreeSum.LayerCounts.leftFiber_card.formal_statement:

      ({p ∈ ThreeSum.LayerCounts.edgeSet L h |
        @Eq.{1} (Finset.{0} (Fin L)) (@Prod.fst.{0, 0} (Finset.{0} (Fin L)) (Finset.{0} (Fin L)) p) S}))

  sorry
ThreeSum.LayerCounts.leftFiber_card.natural_language_statement:
Let $L,h\in\mathbb N$ and fix a subset $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$ with $|S|=h$. In the graph whose edges are ordered pairs of disjoint $h$-element subsets, the number of edges with left endpoint $S$ is

$$
\bigl|\{(S,T):T\subseteq\{0,\ldots,L-1\},\ |T|=h,\ S\cap T=\varnothing\}\bigr|
=\binom{L-h}{h}.
$$

There is no additional requirement that $2h\le L$; when there is insufficient room for a disjoint partner, the binomial coefficient is zero.

This determines the exact vertex degree used in the local-cover graph counts and their numerical bounds.

ThreeSum.LayerCounts.unionFiber_card.natural_language_statement:
Let $L,h\in\mathbb N$ and let $Q\subseteq\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$ have cardinality $2h$. The number of ordered pairs of disjoint $h$-element subsets whose union is $Q$ is

$$
\bigl|\{(S,T):|S|=|T|=h,\ S\cap T=\varnothing,\ S\cup T=Q\}\bigr|
=\binom{2h}{h}.
$$

The pairs are ordered, so exchanging the two subsets is not identified. The statement includes the empty case $h=0$.

This gives the exact number of graph representations of a single output subset, a quantity used in the local hash-cover counting estimates.

ThreeSum.LightBandPreprocessing.time_bou.natural_language_statement:
Let $a,b,c,g\in\mathbb N$ be three class lengths and the band-size parameter, and put $N=a+b+c$. Define $s_g(0)=0$ and $s_g(t)=\lfloor(t-1)/g\rfloor+1$ for $t>0$, using natural division with quotient zero when $g=0$. Put $A=s_g(a)$, $B=s_g(b)$, $C=s_g(c)$, $R=BC+AB+AC$, and $W=\operatorname{clog}_2(A+B+C+1)$, where $\operatorname{clog}_2(t)$ is the least natural $k$ with $t\le2^k$. The declared preprocessing time satisfies

$$
T(a,b,c,g)\le
2100(N+1)(\operatorname{clog}_2(N)+1)
+1000(R+N+1)(W+1)+400.
$$

The two terms account for normalization of the three classes and construction of the rectangular owner tables. This finite estimate exposes the dependence on input length, candidate-table size, and lookup width.

ThreeSum.LightBoxStages.time_bound.natural_language_statement:
Let $L,c$ be natural numbers with $c\le L$, and let
$$D(L,c)=\sum_{r=0}^{c}\binom{L}{r}$$
be the number of masks in the subset downset of cutoff $c$. Let $T_{\mathrm{box}}(L,c)$ be the implementation's time budget for constructing and retaining every prefix-zeta stage, processing coordinates in increasing order. This budget includes downset-size computation, the $L$ zeta passes, and their fixed overhead. Then
$$T_{\mathrm{box}}(L,c)\le 6000(L+1)^4\bigl(D(L,c)+1\bigr).$$

The estimate supplies the preprocessing cost for the retained stages used by canonical box queries.

ThreeSum.LightLocalCoverTransport.choice.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.LightLocalCoverTransport.choices_map : ∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {U : Type u_2} [inst : Inhabited.{u_1 + 1} Ω] [inst_1 : DecidableEq.{u_2 + 1} U]
  (matrix : Nat → Nat → Nat) (candidate : Nat → Ω) (target : Nat → U) (covers : Ω → U → Prop)
  [inst_2 : @DecidableRel.{u_1 + 1, u_2 + 1} Ω U covers] {rows cols : Nat}
  (hrows : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))) rows)
  (hinj :
    @Set.InjOn.{0, u_2} Nat U target
      (@SetLike.coe.{0, 0} (Finset.{0} Nat) Nat (@Finset.instSetLike.{0} Nat) (Finset.range cols)))
  (hcover :
    ∀ (i j : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j cols →
        Iff (ThreeSum.BooleanGreedy.covers matrix i j) (covers (candidate i) (target j)))
  (rounds : Nat),
  @Eq.{u_1 + 1} (List.{u_1} Ω)
    (@List.map.{0, u_1} Nat Ω candidate (ThreeSum.BooleanGreedy.choices matrix rows cols rounds))
    (@ThreeSum.Cover.greedyChoices.{u_1, u_2} Ω U inst (@List.map.{0, u_1} Nat Ω candidate (List.range rows)) covers
      inst_2 (@Finset.image.{0, u_2} Nat U inst_1 target (Finset.range cols)) rounds) := by
  sorry
ThreeSum.LightLocalCoverTransport.choice.natural_language_statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an inhabited candidate type and $U$ a target type with decidable equality. Let $M:\mathbb N^2\to\mathbb N$, $c:\mathbb N\to\Omega$, and $u:\mathbb N\to U$, with a decidable covering relation. Fix $R>0$ rows and $C$ columns. Assume $u$ is injective below $C$ and, for every row index $i$ and $j<C$, $M_{ij}=1$ exactly when $c(i)$ covers $u(j)$. For every number of rounds $t$,

$$
\operatorname{map}(c,\operatorname{BooleanChoices}(M,R,C,t))
=\operatorname{GreedyChoices}([c(0),\ldots,c(R-1)],\{u(j):j<C\},t).
$$

Both greedy procedures break ties by the given list order. Candidate labels may repeat, and matrix entries need not be bounded by one; only equality to one defines coverage. The identity preserves the whole ordered schedule.

ThreeSum.LightMinimum.least_value_le.natural_language_statement:
Let $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$. Define the running-minimum index $m_0=0$ and, recursively, $m_{n+1}=n$ if $f(n)<f(m_n)$, with $m_{n+1}=m_n$ otherwise. For natural numbers $i<n$,

$$f(m_n)\le f(i).$$

The strict update rule keeps the previous index when values tie. This establishes the value comparison needed for the minimum-selection routine.

    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) (Nat.log y M)

ThreeSum.LightPrimeChain.sum_scores_le_l.natural_language_statement:
Let $p_0,\ldots,p_{s-1}$ be distinct primes with $p_i\ge y>1$, and let $q,n_A,n_B,n_C,M$ be natural numbers. Let $A,B,C$ be integer arrays on their respective index ranges. For each triple $(a,b,c)$ in those ranges, put $\delta=C(c)-B(b)-A(a)$ and assume $|\delta|\le M$. Define $w(\delta)$ as the number of these $s$ primes that do not divide $\delta$, and let
$$S(q)=\sum_{a<n_A,\ b<n_B,\ c<n_C}\mathbf1_{q\mid\delta}\,w(\delta).$$
Then
$$\sum_{i=0}^{s-1}S(qp_i)\le\operatorname{log}_y^{\mathbb N}(M)\,S(q),$$
where the integer logarithm is $\lfloor\log_y M\rfloor$ for $M\ge1$ and is zero for $M=0$.

This bounds the aggregate weighted false-triple score over all candidate prime extensions.

ThreeSum.LightPrimePool.prefix_increasin.theorem_title: Every scanned prime prefix is strictly increasing
ThreeSum.LightPrimePool.prefix_increasin.natural_language_statement:
For $y,i\in\mathbb N$, let $S_{y,i}$ be the list obtained by scanning $y+1,\ldots,y+i$ in order and appending exactly the prime values. Then

$$0\le j<k<|S_{y,i}|\quad\Longrightarrow\quad(S_{y,i})_j<(S_{y,i})_k.$$

Thus every scan prefix is strictly increasing, including the empty prefix. This ordering property supports the prime-pool interface and rules out repeated candidate values.

          (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
            (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid))) m J)

ThreeSum.LightRadixKeys.space_bound.natural_language_statement:
Let $d,J\in\mathbb N$ and let $m\ge1$ be a natural number. The positional-key construction stores a length header and an array of $m^j$ keys at each stage $j=0,\ldots,J$, beginning at address $d$. Its declared end address $S(d,m,J)$ satisfies

$$
S(d,m,J)\le d+(J+1)(m^J+1).
$$

The bound includes the headers and all intermediate product stages, not only the final array. Equal key values are still stored as separate entries.

This gives a simple bound on the address range required by the complete Cartesian-product key constructor.

theorem ThreeSum.LightReportingSuffixTable.time_bound : ∀ {W V cut : Nat} (hV : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat V W) (hcut : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat cut V),

    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
      (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 12000) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 12000)))
        (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
          (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid)))
          (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) W
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 3) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 3)))))
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) (ThreeSum.SubsetAddress.downsetCap V cut)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))) := by

ThreeSum.LightReportingSuffixTable.time_.natural_language_statement:
Let $W,V,c\in\mathbb N$ with $c\le V\le W$. Let $D(V,c)=\sum_{r=0}^{c}\binom Vr$ be the number of subsets of the suffix ground set of size at most $c$. The concrete suffix-table construction has time budget

$$
T(W,V,c)\le12000(W+1)^3\bigl(D(V,c)+1\bigr).
$$

The table enumerates the cardinality layers at width $V$ and evaluates them against source transforms of width $W$. The estimate keeps the subset count tied to the shrinking suffix width while allowing polynomial overhead in the full width.

          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))))

ThreeSum.LightSelectedPrime.time_bound.natural_language_statement:
For a natural threshold $N$, let $T_{\mathrm{prime}}(N)$ be the declared time budget of the concrete selected-prime routine. Its budget includes integer square-root computation, scanning the constructed prime-candidate pool with verified primality tests, and the final header lookup. For every $N\in\mathbb N$,

$$
T_{\mathrm{prime}}(N)\le6000(N+2)^3.
$$

This is an inequality for the total budget function, including $N=0$.

The estimate converts the detailed operational cost into a simple polynomial bound used in the local-parameter construction, while accounting for the candidate scan and primality computation explicitly.

ThreeSum.LightSourceOccurrenceArray.time.natural_language_statement:
Let $N,J\in\mathbb N$ be the number of bank indices and the number of radix digits stored for each index. Let $T(N,J)$ be the defined time budget of the occurrence-array routine, which invokes the logarithmic quotient-based decoder once for each row. Then

$$T(N,J)\le300(N+1)(J+1)\bigl(\log_2^{\mathrm{nat}}(N+1)+2\bigr),$$

where $\log_2^{\mathrm{nat}}$ is the natural-number floor logarithm. This bound charges all decoded coordinates and loop overhead, including the zero-size cases, to the source-catalog construction.

ThreeSum.LightZetaStages.time_bound.natural_language_statement:
Let $L,c$ be natural numbers with $c\le L$, and write
$$D(L,c)=\sum_{r=0}^{c}\binom{L}{r}$$
for the number of masks of cardinality at most $c$. Let $T_{\mathrm{zeta}}(L,c)$ be the implementation's time budget for constructing and retaining all suffix-zeta stages, processing coordinates in decreasing order. The budget includes downset-size setup, $L$ zeta passes, and fixed loop overhead. Then
$$T_{\mathrm{zeta}}(L,c)\le 6000(L+1)^4\bigl(D(L,c)+1\bigr).$$

This bounds the source-stage preprocessing used to answer queries with a forced prefix and a remaining suffix.

ThreeSum.LocalCoverBounds.pow_le_choose_.natural_language_statement:
For arbitrary natural numbers $c$ and $r$,

$$
c^r\le \binom{cr}{r}.
$$

The right side counts all subsets of size $r$ in a set of $cr$ positions. The left side counts choices of one position in each of $r$ labeled blocks, each containing $c$ positions. The assertion also includes $c=0$ and $r=0$, with the usual natural-number conventions for powers and binomial coefficients.

This exact finite estimate supplies a lower bound for the number of local subset outputs without using asymptotic factorial estimates.

ThreeSum.LocalHashMoments.cover_frequenc.natural_language_statement:
Let $K$ be a finite field of cardinality $q$, and let $h,L\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $2h<L$. Write $\Delta=\binom{L-h}{h}$, $G=\binom{2h}{h}$, $O=\binom{L}{2h}$, and $B=\lceil4(q+\binom Lh)/q\rceil$. Assume $\Delta\le q$, $G\le q$, $OG\le q^2$, and $q^2\le16O2^{2h}$.

For any target $(u,v)\in K^2$, a weight assignment consists of two field coordinates at each of the $L$ positions. It covers the target if some ordered disjoint pair of $h$-subsets has the two required one-hot hashes and both corresponding hash buckets have size at most $B$. Then
$$q^{2L}\le320(2h+1)\,\#\{w:w\text{ covers }(u,v)\}.$$

Thus each target is covered by a polynomial fraction of the concrete weight space under the stated finite parameter inequalities.

ThreeSum.LocalHashMoments.hitCount_cap.natural_language_statement:
Let $K$ be a finite field, let $L,h,B\in\mathbb N$, and assign weights $w:\{0,\ldots,L-1\}\times\{0,1\}\to K$. The local graph has ordered pairs of disjoint $h$-subsets as edges, with the left word equal to one on its subset and the right word equal to zero on its subset. A word $s$ has hash $\sum_i w(i,s(i))$. Fix any target $(a,b)\in K^2$. Count edges whose endpoint hashes are $a,b$ and whose corresponding left and right hash buckets both contain at most $B$ vertices. This retained hit count satisfies

$$
\operatorname{hits}_{L,h,B}(w;a,b)\le B^2.
$$

The two target values may be equal, and no positivity or separation hypothesis on $L,h,B$ is required.

This supplies a pointwise representation cap for every retained target, complementing the averaged hash-moment estimates.

ThreeSum.OutputDecodeOrder.indices_getD_.natural_language_statement:
For natural numbers $m,J,k$, define an index list recursively by $D_{m,0}(k)=[]$ and $D_{m,J+1}(k)=D_{m,J}(k\mathbin{/}m)\mathbin{+\!+}[k\bmod m]$, where division is natural-number division. For every $j<J$,

$$
D_{m,J}(k)[J-1-j]=\left(\frac{k}{m^j}\right)\bmod m.
$$

List access is the default-zero access used by the decoder, though the indicated position is valid. No positivity assumption on $m$ or bound on $k$ is needed; the natural division and remainder conventions apply at zero. This identifies each physical tuple index with its positional digit.

ThreeSum.OutputDecodeOrder.tuples_getD_i.natural_language_statement:
Let $A=[a_0,\ldots,a_{m-1}]$ be a nonempty list of elements of any type, and let $J,k\in\mathbb N$ with $k<m^J$. Enumerate all length-$J$ tuples from this list in the product order with the first coordinate outermost. Let $(d_0,\ldots,d_{J-1})$ be the length-$J$ base-$m$ digit list of $k$, with leading zeros and the last digit obtained by remainder. Then

$$
\operatorname{tuples}(A,J)[k]=[a_{d_0},\ldots,a_{d_{J-1}}].
$$

The formal lookup may use any default element; the index bounds ensure it is never needed. Repeated values in $A$ are allowed.

This ties quotient/remainder decoding to exact physical enumeration order rather than merely to the set of tuple values.

Let $C$ be a finite set of natural primes, let $y>1$ be a natural number, and assume $p\ge y$ for every $p\in C$. For any nonzero integer $z$,

ThreeSum.PrimeChain.sum_scores_le.theorem_title: Averaging bound for weighted modular scores
ThreeSum.PrimeChain.sum_scores_le.natural_language_statement:
Let $T$ be a finite index set, $d:T\to\mathbb Z$ an integer difference assignment, and $w:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb N$ a weight function with $w(0)=0$. For $q\in\mathbb N$, set $S(q)=\sum_{i\in T,\ q\mid |d(i)|}w(d(i))$. Let $C\subseteq\mathbb N$ be finite and $K\in\mathbb N$. Suppose each nonzero $d(i)$ is divisible in absolute value by at most $K$ members of $C$. Then

$$
\sum_{p\in C}S(qp)\le K S(q).
$$

Neither primality of the members of $C$ nor positivity of $q$ is required. Zero differences contribute no weight, so the estimate remains valid when genuine zero-sum witnesses are present.

Let $\Omega$ be a finite type with decidable equality, let $p\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, and let $\ell,r:\Omega\to\mathbb Z$ be endpoint maps. For a list $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{s-1})$, define the low-digit-first positional hash $H_u(x)=\sum_{i<s}p^i u(x_i)$.

The recursive family $R_j(a,b)$ chooses a first symbol whose two endpoint differences are divisible by $p$, then recurses on the quotient targets; $R_0(a,b)=\{[]\}$. For all natural $j$, integer targets $a,b$, and lists $x$,
$$
x\in R_j(a,b)\iff |x|=j\ \land\ p^j\mid a-H_\ell(x)\ \land\ p^j\mid b-H_r(x).
$$
This identifies the recursive candidate family with exactly the simultaneous positional congruences, including the original local choices.

ThreeSum.Radix.radix_divisibility.natural_language_statement:
Let $p,a,h,t\in\mathbb Z$ with $p\ne0$, and let $j\in\mathbb N$. Divisibility through one positional digit satisfies

$$
p^{j+1}\mid a-(h+pt)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
p\mid a-h\ \text{ and }\ p^j\mid\frac{a-h}{p}-t.
$$

The quotient is integer division; on the right, the first divisibility condition makes it exact. The radix may be negative, and the statement includes $j=0$.

This algebraic equivalence underlies the recursive radix representation rule, determining the next quotient target from the current digit without introducing an independent carry choice.

ThreeSum.Radix.representations_card_le.natural_language_statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, $p\in\mathbb Z$, and $\ell,r:\Omega\to\mathbb Z$. Suppose every local fiber
$F(a,b)=\{\omega:p\mid a-\ell(\omega),\ p\mid b-r(\omega)\}$ has at most $B\in\mathbb N$ elements. Define the recursive representation set $R_0(a,b)=\{[]\}$; at the next level, choose $\omega\in F(a,b)$ and recurse on the quotient targets $(a-\ell(\omega))/p$ and $(b-r(\omega))/p$. Then for all $j\in\mathbb N$ and $a,b\in\mathbb Z$,

$$
|R_j(a,b)|\le B^j.
$$

The definition uses total integer division, with quotient zero when $p=0$; no nonzero-radix assumption is needed for this counting statement.

The estimate bounds global representation multiplicity without adding a separate branching factor for carries.

$$
\operatorname{Nodup}(B)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Nodup}(\mathcal T_j(B)).

$$

Let the child list at each depth contain every symbol appearing there in these words, and assume every child list has no repetitions. $$
Q(j,u)=\sum_{\substack{i\in I\\\operatorname{take}_j(w_i)=u}}a_i.

$$
|\operatorname{frontier}_k|\le\sum_{i\in I}a_i.
$$
This bounds the number of visited prefixes even when distinct incidences have identical words.

ThreeSum.Reporting.mem_frontier_iff.natural_language_statement:
Let $I$ be a finite incidence set with words $w_i$ over an alphabet with decidable equality and natural weights $a_i$. Suppose every $w_i$ has length $J$, its symbol at position $j<J$ belongs to the supplied child list $C_j$, and every query through depth $J$ equals the exact prefix mass

$$M_k(P)=\sum_{i\in I:\,\operatorname{take}_k(w_i)=P}a_i.$$

Let $F_k$ be the frontier formed by repeatedly appending supplied children and filtering for positive query values. For $k\le J$ and every prefix $P$,

$$P\in F_k\iff M_k(P)>0.$$

This proves both soundness and completeness of positive-prefix reporting. Duplicate child entries are allowed in this membership theorem.

ThreeSum.ReportingHostMasks.blockSet_loc.theorem_title: Local coordinates reconstruct any subset of a single block
ThreeSum.ReportingHostMasks.blockSet_loc.natural_language_statement:
Let $J,L\in\mathbb N$, fix a block $i<J$, and let $Q\subseteq\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$. Write $B_i(Q)=\{iL+a:a\in Q\}$. If a global set $T\subseteq\{0,\ldots,JL-1\}$ satisfies $T\subseteq B_i(Q)$, let $\operatorname{row}_i(T)$ collect its local coordinates in block $i$. Then

$$B_i\bigl(\operatorname{row}_i(T)\bigr)=T.$$

This inverse relation allows a child subset enumerated in the global address space to be interpreted as a local reporting row without losing any elements.

Let $k:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be injective on indices below $n$, and let $S$ be a nondecreasing integer list that is a permutation of the packed codes $k(j)(n+1)+j$ for $j<n$. Fix $i<n$, and let $K$ be the upper-bound search position in $S$ for the threshold $k(i)(n+1)+n$. Then

$$
0<K\le n,\qquad S_{K-1}=k(i)(n+1)+i.
$$

Thus the last code below the requested key's interval ceiling is exactly its original record. The low digit retains the unchanged physical catalog index despite sorting.

ThreeSum.ReportingHostPairEnumeration.le.theorem_title: Every valid left-subset enumeration index selects an h-element set
ThreeSum.ReportingHostPairEnumeration.le.natural_language_statement:
Let $L,h,i$ be natural numbers, and let $S_i$ be the subset obtained by decoding position $i$ in the enumeration of $L$-bit masks of weight $h$. If $i<\binom{L}{h}$, then
$$|S_i|=h.$$
Here the selected subset is a subset of $\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$, and the index hypothesis ensures that the enumeration's default value is not used.

This validates the cardinality of the left component selected by the pair-enumeration host.

ThreeSum.ReportingHostPairEnumeration.pa.theorem_title: The disjoint h-subset pair enumeration has an exact binomial length
ThreeSum.ReportingHostPairEnumeration.pa.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.ReportingHostPairEnumeration.pairs_length : ∀ (L h : Nat),
  @Eq.{1} Nat
    (@List.length.{0} (Prod.{0, 0} (Finset.{0} (Fin L)) (Finset.{0} (Fin L)))
      (ThreeSum.ReportingHostPairEnumeration.pairs L h))
    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
      (L.choose
        (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))) h))
      ((@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))) h).choose
        h)) := by
  sorry
ThreeSum.ReportingHostPairEnumeration.pa.natural_language_statement:
For natural numbers $L,h$, enumerate all $h$-element subsets $S$ of $\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$ and, for each $S$, enumerate all $h$-element subsets $R$ of its complement. Let $P(L,h)$ be the resulting list of ordered pairs $(S,R)$. Then
$$|P(L,h)|=\binom{L}{2h}\binom{2h}{h}.$$
The equality uses the usual convention that $\binom{L}{2h}=0$ when $2h>L$.

This gives the exact number of entries required for the host's list of balanced disjoint subset pairs.

ThreeSum.ReportingHostPairEnumeration.ri.natural_language_statement:
Let $L,h\in\mathbb N$, and let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$ have cardinality $h$. The right-subset enumeration lists the $h$-element subsets of the complement of $S$. Its length is

$$
|\operatorname{rights}(S,h)|=\binom{L-h}{h}.
$$

The formula includes the case where the complement has fewer than $h$ elements, when the list is empty. It supplies the exact row length for enumerating disjoint balanced pairs.

ThreeSum.Scales.primeDepth_loss_bound.theorem_title: Finite modulus loss from the selected prime-chain depth
ThreeSum.Scales.primeDepth_loss_bound.natural_language_statement:
Let $R:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be any target-radix function. For $n\in\mathbb N$, put $m=\operatorname{inputBits}(n)$, $y=2^{\lfloor\sqrt m\rfloor+1}$, and $r=\operatorname{ilog}_{4y}(R(n)\mathbin{\mathrm{div}}4)$, where the integer logarithm is zero on argument zero. If a natural number $P$ satisfies $y^r\le P$, then

$$
R(n)\le32y\,4^r P.
$$

        @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat

              (@Finset.instSDiff.{u_1} α fun (a b : α) => @LinearOrder.toDecidableEq.{u_1} α inst a b) q leaf))

        weight leaf)

        @ThreeSum.SparseBoxes.boxSum.{u_1} α inst
          (@SDiff.sdiff.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α)
            (@Finset.instSDiff.{u_1} α fun (a b : α) => @LinearOrder.toDecidableEq.{u_1} α inst a b) q u)

ThreeSum.SparseBoxes.sparse_query_identi.natural_language_statement:
Let $q$ be a finite subset of a linearly ordered type, let $t\in\mathbb N$, and let $w$ assign an integer weight to each finite subset. For $u\subseteq q$, define $F(q,u)=\{x\in q\setminus u:\forall y\in u,\ x<y\}$. Let $B(A,F)$ denote the sum of $w(\ell)$ over $A\setminus F\subseteq\ell\subseteq A$. Then

$$
\sum_{\ell\subseteq q}w(\ell)
=\sum_{\substack{\ell\subseteq q\\|q\setminus\ell|<t}}w(\ell)
+\sum_{\substack{u\subseteq q\\|u|=t}}B(q\setminus u,F(q,u)).
$$

This exact identity separates the near-full subsets into explicit accesses and all remaining subsets into canonical box queries. It holds for signed weights and every threshold, including zero.

Let $f,g$ be integer-valued functions on finite subsets of a type with decidable equality, supported respectively on sets of cardinalities $a,b$. Define $Z_Sf(U)=\sum_{X\subseteq U\cap S}f((U\setminus S)\cup X)$ and $\mathcal MH(Q)=\sum_{T\subseteq Q}(-1)^{|Q|-|T|}H(T)$. Then
$$
\mathcal M\!\left(T\mapsto Z_Sf(P_1\cup T)Z_Sg(P_2\cup T)\right)(Q)
=\sum_{X\subseteq Q}f(P_1\cup X)g(P_2\cup(Q\setminus X)).
$$

ThreeSum.Subset.unionConvolution_eq_disj.natural_language_statement:

ThreeSum.SubsetAddress.enumerateLayer_no.natural_language_statement:
For $L,k\in\mathbb N$, let $E_{L,k}$ be the recursively constructed list of $L$-bit masks having $k$ selected positions. The enumeration visits the lower half before the upper half and stops on empty layers. It has no repeated entries:

$$
\forall i,j<|E_{L,k}|,\qquad
E_{L,k}[i]=E_{L,k}[j]\Longrightarrow i=j.
$$

The assertion is uniform in $L$ and $k$: the zero-weight list contains only the zero mask, and layers with $k>L$ are empty.

This uniqueness property allows list positions to serve as unambiguous compact addresses for subsets of a fixed size.

ThreeSum.WeightEnumeration.pi_eq_range.theorem_title: Ordered Cartesian enumeration equals radix decoding
ThreeSum.WeightEnumeration.pi_eq_range.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.WeightEnumeration.pi_eq_range : ∀ {ι : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq.{u_1 + 1} ι] [inst_1 : NatCast.{u_2} K] (p : Nat)
  (l : List.{u_1} ι),
  @Eq.{max (u_1 + 1) (u_2 + 1)}
    (List.{max u_1 u_2} ((i : ι) → @Membership.mem.{u_1, u_1} ι (List.{u_1} ι) (@List.instMembership.{u_1} ι) l i → K))
    (@List.pi.{u_1, u_2} ι inst (fun (x : ι) => K) l fun (x : ι) =>
      @List.map.{0, u_2} Nat K (fun (n : Nat) => @Nat.cast.{u_2} K inst_1 n) (List.range p))
    (@List.map.{0, max u_1 u_2} Nat
      ((i : ι) → @Membership.mem.{u_1, u_1} ι (List.{u_1} ι) (@List.instMembership.{u_1} ι) l i → K)
      (@ThreeSum.WeightEnumeration.decode.{u_1, u_2} ι K inst inst_1 p l)
      (List.range
        (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
          (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid))) p
          (@List.length.{u_1} ι l)))) := by
  sorry
ThreeSum.WeightEnumeration.pi_eq_range.natural_language_statement:
Let $\iota$ be an index type with decidable equality, and let $K$ carry a specified natural-number cast $c:\mathbb N\to K$. Let $p\in\mathbb N$ and let $l$ be a finite list of indices. Form the ordered Cartesian-product list $\Pi_l$ by choosing each coordinate from $[c(0),\ldots,c(p-1)]$, with the first list position varying most slowly. Let $D_{p,l}(k)$ be the recursive decoder that reads the most significant digit first; repeated labels use their first occurrence. Then

$$\Pi_l=\bigl[D_{p,l}(0),D_{p,l}(1),\ldots,D_{p,l}(p^{|l|}-1)\bigr].$$

This is equality of lists, including their order and repetitions. It identifies the original coefficient enumeration with concrete radix indices without assuming distinct labels or an injective cast.

ThreeSum.WeightedScore.score_eq_remainin.theorem_title: The weighted modular score equals the final correction remainder
ThreeSum.WeightedScore.score_eq_remainin.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.WeightedScore.score_eq_remaining : ∀ (primes : Nat → Nat) (s q nA nB nC : Nat) (a b c : Nat → Int)
  (hprime : ∀ (i : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i s → Nat.Prime (primes i))
  (hinj :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i s →
        ∀ (j : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j s → @Eq.{1} Nat (primes i) (primes j) → @Eq.{1} Nat i j),
  @Eq.{1} Nat (ThreeSum.WeightedScore.score primes s q nA nB nC a b c)
    (ThreeSum.WeightedScore.remaining primes s q nA nB nC a b c s) := by
  sorry
ThreeSum.WeightedScore.score_eq_remainin.natural_language_statement:
Let $a,b,c:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ have specified lengths $n_A,n_B,n_C$, and let $p_0,\ldots,p_{s-1}$ be pairwise distinct natural primes. Let $N_m$ count index triples in these lengths for which $m\mid c_k-b_j-a_i$. Define $J(q,p)=q$ if $p\mid q$, and $J(q,p)=qp$ otherwise. The weighted score counts each triple divisible by $q$ with weight equal to the number of auxiliary primes that do not divide its difference. For any $q\in\mathbb N$,

$$
\operatorname{score}=sN_q-\sum_{j=0}^{s-1}N_{J(q,p_j)}
=\operatorname{remaining}(s).
$$

Subtraction is the natural-number subtraction of the defined correction accumulator. This matches the score specification with the array-ordered correction computation, including shared factors with $q$.
